# Release compatibility table

<!-- Generated by `node scripts/release/compat-table.mjs --write` from design/compatibility/seed.json and release.packages.json; do not edit. -->

Names are the `target` namespace of release.packages.json (pending [issue 41](https://github.com/baseten/pixi-react/issues/41)). **Tested** means: covered by the PR-tier cells of the [#13 matrix](compatibility/cells/COMPATIBILITY.md), the required check on every pull request. **Verified** means, per render backend (WebGL and WebGPU are checked separately): the tuple's nightly cell passed on that backend in a dated [verification record](compatibility/verification/) whose boundary probes and incompatible pairs all behaved as expected; the exact tuples are `verifiedRanges` in the manifest. Verification is evidence, not a support guarantee, and never widens a peer range (see [release.md](release.md#tested-and-verified)).

**Rendering.** Record [2026-10-10-macos-26-apple-m5-max](compatibility/verification/2026-10-10-macos-26-apple-m5-max.md): Real GPU: ANGLE (Apple, ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M5 Max, Unspecified Version); apple / metal-3, isFallbackAdapter false. The render check confirmed no backend ran on a software renderer or a fallback adapter. Record [2026-10-10.2](compatibility/verification/2026-10-10.2.md): Software rendering: no GPU took part. WebGL ran on ANGLE over SwiftShader and WebGPU on Dawn over SwiftShader's Vulkan device, a fallback adapter (isFallbackAdapter true). It counts as verification; a run on a real GPU (run-cells.mjs --gpu hardware) can be added later as extra evidence.

WebGPU with pixi.js 8.2.6 … 8.9.2 (8 versions) (pixi-8, software rendering) is an **expected blank render, unverified**: An upstream pixi.js bug before 8.10 (pixijs/pixijs#11389, fixed by #11417, first released in 8.10.0): the WebGPU texture batch is sized from WebGL's MAX_TEXTURE_IMAGE_UNITS (32 on ANGLE/SwiftShader) while the WebGPU device keeps the default maxSampledTexturesPerShaderStage of 16, so the bind group layout and the batch pipeline are invalid and the canvas stays blank (reads [0,0,0,0]) although Pixi creates a WebGPU renderer and every conformance scenario passes. It is not specific to software rendering: any device whose WebGL texture-unit count exceeds its WebGPU per-stage limit is affected (upstream reports a Pixel 9 and Chrome on Ubuntu). Not in the adapters. Bisected with the pixi.js bundles on the same adapter: 8.2.6, 8.9.0, 8.9.2 and 8.9.2-dev.f4f8fb2 blank; 8.9.2-dev.89285a6 (the merge of #11417), 8.10.0, 8.10.1 and 8.10.2 render. First good release: 8.10.0. A real GPU renders these versions when its WebGL and WebGPU texture limits agree: the full hardware record 2026-10-10-macos-26-apple-m5-max (Apple M5 Max, Metal, isFallbackAdapter false; WebGL reports 16 texture units there) passed 8.2.6 to 8.9.2 on WebGPU with every React adapter at both audited patches, so those tuples are verified on WebGPU with the known issue adapterMatrix.knownIssues pixi8-webgpu-texture-limit-before-8.10 beside them (owner ruling: verified + known issue). The blank render here is the #11389 limit mismatch of SwiftShader's fallback adapter, which that Mac does not have, not WebGPU on 8.2-8.9 as such.

## The facade

| `@pixi/react` | React peer | React tested | pixi.js peer | pixi.js tested on every PR | pixi.js in the nightly cells | Verified (the adapter packages it builds in) | Builds in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8.1.0 (Release 1, not yet published) | `^19.3.0` | 19.3.0 | `>=8.2.6 <8.5.0 \|\| >=8.5.1 <8.23.0` | 8.2.6, 8.22.0 | 21 versions: the newest audited patch of each minor, 8.2.6 … 8.22.0 | WebGL: React 19.3.0 × pixi.js 8.2.6 … 8.22.0 (21 versions). WebGPU: React 19.3.0 × pixi.js 8.2.6 … 8.22.0 (21 versions) (**Known issue** (pixi.js before 8.10.0 on WebGPU): some devices render a blank canvas on WebGPU: pixi.js before 8.10 sizes the WebGPU texture batch from WebGL's texture-unit count, which exceeds the WebGPU per-stage limit on those devices ([pixijs/pixijs#11389](https://github.com/pixijs/pixijs/issues/11389), [pixijs/pixijs#11417](https://github.com/pixijs/pixijs/pull/11417); fixed in 8.10.0); use pixi.js 8.10 or later for WebGPU, or WebGL.) (records [2026-10-10-macos-26-apple-m5-max](compatibility/verification/2026-10-10-macos-26-apple-m5-max.md), [2026-10-10.2](compatibility/verification/2026-10-10.2.md)) | `@pixi/react-19.3` 8.1.0, `@pixi/react-pixi-8` 8.1.0; react-reconciler 0.34.0, its-fine 2.1.1 |
| 8.0.5 (upstream, for comparison) | `>=19.0.0` | - | `^8.2.6` | - | - | - | react-reconciler 0.31.0 (the React 19.0 epoch), its-fine ^2.0.0 |

On a React 19 minor other than 19.3 the facade installs (its peer is a caret range), runs and logs one warning; pixi.js 8.5.0 is excluded from the range.

Every package releases at the facade's version (8.1.0), and a dependency between our packages names exactly that version: install all `@pixi/react-*` packages at the same version (see [release.md](release.md#lockstep-versions)).

`@pixi/react-pixi-7` targets pixi.js `>=7.2.0 <7.4.0 \|\| >=7.4.2 <7.5.0` but releases at the facade's version like every package; the facade itself composes the default Pixi adapter and stays on its Pixi major.
